prompt:
You are a decision-support tool for a radiologist. Review this patient's frontal chest X-ray and report on six findings. A radiologist checks your output; give your best assessment.

Findings and their definitions:
- Lung Opacity: airspace opacity, consolidation, infiltrate or airspace disease in the lung. A discrete nodule or mass is not Lung Opacity (it is Lung Lesion).
- Cardiomegaly: an enlarged heart. A borderline or upper-normal heart size counts as absent.
- Atelectasis: collapse or incomplete expansion of lung tissue, including subsegmental or plate-like atelectasis.
- Lung Lesion: a nodule, mass or cavity in the lung. A calcified granuloma does not count.
- Pleural Effusion: fluid in the pleural space.
- Fracture: a fracture of the ribs, clavicles, spine or any other visible bone. Healed or old fractures count.

How to work:
1. Read the patient's image systematically first.
2. Then look at the 10 most similar cases from a reference database, listed below with their reports. They are other patients whose images look similar to this one. Use them as supporting evidence to confirm or question what you see in the patient's image, not as the answer: a finding in a similar case does not mean that this patient has it.
3. For each of the six findings, give its status (present, absent or uncertain), the probability (0 to 1) that it is present in this patient, the IDs of the similar cases that support your call (an empty list if none), and a rationale of one or two sentences. Then give a short impression. Do not explain what the findings are. Cite cases by their ID exactly as written, e.g. CXR316. Give the probability with two decimals as your honest estimate; for subtle, borderline or partly obscured appearances, use intermediate values rather than a fixed low value.

Similar cases (most similar first):
Case CXR2918 (similarity 0.948): FINDINGS: Cardiomediastinal silhouette is normal. Pulmonary vasculature and XXXX are normal. No consolidation, pneumothorax or large pleural effusion. Osseous structures and soft tissues are normal. IMPRESSION: No acute cardiopulmonary disease.
Case CXR3534 (similarity 0.922): FINDINGS: Lungs are clear bilaterally. There is no focal consolidation, pleural effusion, or pneumothoraces. Heart size is normal. Stable right paratracheal prominence, consistent with known calcified lymph node, seen on prior CT chest dated XXXX. XXXX are unremarkable. IMPRESSION: No acute cardiopulmonary abnormality.
Case CXR703 (similarity 0.920): IMPRESSION: Heart size normal. Mediastinal silhouette and vascularity are within normal limits. Lungs are clear, hyperinflated. There is no pleural effusion or pneumothorax.
Case CXR379 (similarity 0.917): FINDINGS: There has been interval placement of a dual-lumen dialysis catheter with the distal tip projected over the right atrium. Moderate cardiomegaly is identified. There is mild calcification of the transverse XXXX. XXXX airspace opacities are identified with bilateral pleural effusions. IMPRESSION: 1. Interval placement of a dual-lumen dialysis catheter with the distal tip projected over the right atrium. 2. Bibasilar airspace opacities and bilateral pleural effusions.
Case CXR1615 (similarity 0.915): no report text
Case CXR700 (similarity 0.913): FINDINGS: The heart is normal in size and contour. There is a calcified granuloma in the right lower lung. The lungs are clear, without evidence of infiltrate. There is no pneumothorax or effusion. Osteopenia with mild degenerative changes of the thoracic spine is noted. IMPRESSION: Stable appearance of the chest. No acute findings.
Case CXR784 (similarity 0.910): FINDINGS: Normal heart size. Tortuous calcified aorta. Scattered granulomas. No lobar pneumonia. Probable XXXX post your recess effusions. Kyphotic degenerated osteopenic thoracic spine. IMPRESSION: Probable XXXX posterior recess effusions with mild basilar atelectasis. No lobar pneumonia.
Case CXR3250 (similarity 0.907): FINDINGS: Lungs are relatively clear. Heart size normal. Unfolded aorta. Moderate hiatal hernia. T-spine osteophytes and DISH. IMPRESSION: Moderate hiatal hernia. No definite pneumonia.
Case CXR2276 (similarity 0.907): FINDINGS: This radiograph was XXXX available for my interpretation at XXXX hours XXXX/XXXX. There are low lung volumes with associated bronchovascular crowding and basilar subsegmental atelectasis. The cardiomediastinal silhouette and pulmonary vasculature are within normal limits. There is no pneumothorax or pleural effusion. There are no focal areas of consolidation. IMPRESSION: No acute cardiopulmonary abnormality.
Case CXR1818 (similarity 0.907): IMPRESSION: Very low lung volumes, bronchovascular crowding and bibasilar areas of atelectasis. No lobar consolidation. No appreciable pleural effusion or pneumothorax. Heart size within normal limits.

The patient's frontal chest X-ray follows.
